# Standards map — tables and related columns

What this is: one row per rule (or definition/cross-reference) of BANA Braille Formats 2016 §11 and UKAAF B004 §12, quoted verbatim from `references/_text/`, with what it requires, whether it's mechanically testable, Emboss's status, the function(s)/line(s) that are the evidence for that status, and the tests that prove it (or "none" when no existing test does). Worked examples get their own table further down, since they illustrate rules rather than state them; their own status/tests/evidence columns were added at Stage 2 (they did not exist at Stage 1).

How rows are identified: ids follow the standard's own numbering (`BANA 11.3.2a`, `B004 12a`) where the source numbers/letters an item; where the source gives no label (a few unlettered B004 sentences, and BANA's worked examples), the id is a short, descriptive tag instead (e.g. `B004 12 guide-dots`, `BANA Sample 11-3`) and its row's notes say so. Every id, and every field in this map, also appears in `compare-tables/rules.merged.json` (the machine-readable source this map is generated from), with `sources` (which of the two independent extraction runs, A and/or B, covered it) and `resolution` (why, when the two runs disagreed — see `compare-tables/differences.md` for the full account of every disagreement and how it was settled by re-reading the cited source lines).

This section (the pilot): **216** rule/definition/cross-reference rows (195 BANA, 21 B004 — 9 §12 + 12 Appendix E) and **40** worked examples (36 BANA, 4 B004 — 2 §12 + 2 Appendix E). Stage 2 (Assess, 17 Sep 2026): every row now carries a status (done / partial / not done / out of scope / not-applicable — the map used "not-applicable" at Stage 1 for headings/definitions/cross-references, so it is kept distinct from Stage 2's own "out of scope" for rules that describe a human/transcriber judgement no program should make), the code evidence for that status, and the test(s) that prove it, or "none" (a real gap) / "not tried" (with the reason, for worked examples not run against Emboss). Findings — every partial/not-done status, and every example that doesn't match — are written up in `standards-findings.md`; open questions for a transcriber are in `standards-questions.md`. Appendix E ("Tables") was added 17 Sep 2026, after the original §12 pilot flagged it as unresolved — see "UKAAF B004, Appendix E — Tables" below. Stage 4 (Run and sort, 17 Sep 2026): all 36 BANA §11 worked examples were actually built from `print` and run through Emboss (`Emboss/scripts/gold-run.mjs`, real liblouis translation, BANA 40×25) and diffed against `braille.lines`; the 34 examples with braille were all "not tried" until now — the worked-examples table's "Emboss status" cell for each now also records `(tried, Stage 4: <result>)` and the Evidence cell a one-line cause, cross-referenced to `standards-findings.md`. Current truth lives in `Emboss/tests/gold/bana-formats-2016/section-11/status.json` (produced by, never hand-edited ahead of, the runner) and is guarded by `Emboss/tests/gold_bana_section11.test.mjs`. Headline result at first run: 0 of 34 examples with braille matched byte-for-byte once the gold corpus's own inverted letter-case convention is normalised (see `standards-findings.md` F-24 — a Stage-3 transcription artifact, not an Emboss defect); 4 `not-representable` (a 2-row column-spanning header, F-12) and 30 `mismatch`, dominated by three causes: no code decided table-heading placement relative to a box's top line (F-4, "before or after ... follow print" — the print schema here doesn't even record which one the book used), only one of BANA's six wide-table alternate formats exists (F-18 — facing pages/vertical division/interchange/linear/stairstep all fall back to columnar or Listed), and a hardcoded 2-cell inter-column gutter narrowed to 1 cell in the standard's own examples whenever an entry exactly fills its column (F-10, then newly observed, classification "standard unclear"). **17 Sep 2026, F-4/F-10 fixed** (per Paul's decisions, `EMBOSS-TASKS.md` T7/T8): example-11-2 now `match`es exactly; the other 33 still don't (each blocked by at least one *other*, separate, already-tracked gap — F-11/F-12/F-18 chiefly — that this fix didn't touch), but the heading/caption/box-line placement and gutter causes above are resolved as *mechanisms*, checked by hand against several of the samples they were blocking (see `standards-findings.md` F-4/F-10 "Status update" for the full account). 1 `match`, 4 `not-representable`, 29 `mismatch`, 2 `no-braille`.

## Unresolved — for Paul

1. **Should Appendix E ("Tables", B004, starting at line 434, right after this section's own closing cross-reference to it) be pulled into this pilot?** — **Resolved, 17 Sep 2026: yes**, done. See the "UKAAF B004, Appendix E — Tables" section above (12 rows, 2 worked examples), the two gold files in `Emboss/tests/gold/ukaaf-b004/appendix-e/`, finding F-25, and `standards-questions.md` Q-6/Q-7. (Original note, kept for context: both independent extraction runs of §12 itself had stopped at line 433 because the task specified reading §12 "to the next numbered section", and B004 has no numbered §13 — the table of contents lists sections 1–12 only, followed by the unnumbered "Appendix - Supplementary guidelines", of which E is Tables.)

2. **Does Example 2's own worked braille actually satisfy its own stated rule ("The rows on the facing pages must line up")?** Measured directly from the PDF's line geometry (not just `references/_text/B004.txt`, which has a related but separate spacing artifact of its own — see `differences.md` §3): the left-hand facing page's five day-rows have zero blank lines between them; the right-hand facing page's rows each have one blank line between them. The two pages' rows do not start on the same line, and the gap widens by one line for every row down the table. This was checked against the actual rendered dot/text image, not assumed from the extraction. Is this a genuine erratum in B004's own guide (worth reporting upstream), a convention not documented in the rule text, or simply an artifact of the guide's own typesetting with no normative weight? This decides whether Emboss should ever be tested for exact line-for-line alignment against this particular example. See `standards-map.md`'s `B004 E ex2-align-rows` row and `standards-questions.md` Q-7.

## UKAAF B004, §10 + Appendix C — Lists
(`references/_text/B004.txt`, lines 256–283 (§10, "Lists") and 482–505 (Appendix, "C. Lists"); 5 rule/definition/cross-reference rows + 4 worked examples = 9 rows total. This section has no lettered sub-rules of its own — a guiding-principles paragraph, an "N.B.", and an alternative-practice paragraph in §10 (each with its own "Good practice example", carrying no braille rendering — prose layout description only); a nested-list definition/requirement paragraph in Appendix C (with its own two "Good practice example" margin schemes, also prose-only) — so every id below except the two numbered/lettered section titles is a short descriptive tag, not the standard's own numbering, matching the convention already used for B004 §12's own unlettered sentences and B004 Appendix E's own titled rows. ## Unresolved — for Paul (§8 Lists)

Both items were settled on 17 Sep 2026 by reading the PDF page images (offset: PDF page = printed page + 196 in §8):

1. **`BANA Example 8-7`** (PDF p. 206, page 8-10): the print outline is all-decimal — 1 / 1.1 / 1.2 / 1.2.1 / 2 / 2.1 — so `#a4b4a` is "1.2.1" (UEB numeric mode continues through a full stop; the letters after `4` are digits). Run A was right; the comparison pass's "1.b.a." and Run B's "1.b.i." were wrong. `rules.merged.json` corrected.
2. **`BANA Example 8-8` / `8-9`** (PDF p. 207, page 8-11): the trailing code is `⠼⠁⠑` = `#ae` = braille page 15, at the right margin of line 25. The `.txt` is verbatim; Run A's "(30)" and Run B's "25" were glosses, not readings.

## Unresolved — for Paul (§1)

All three settled on 17 Sep 2026 (method conventions, not rule readings):

1. **Blank cells.** Braille arrays in the reconciled rule files keep the source's U+2800 verbatim; the gold files built from them at Stage 3 store plain spaces (the runner compares spaces), exactly as the §11 and §4 gold files do. No redo needed.
2. **Lead-in sentences before lettered sub-items** are classified by what they say, row by row (a lead-in that itself states a requirement is `exact`/`judgement`; a pure introduction is `not-applicable`) — the reading the comparison already made stands; the §11 rows 11.2.2/11.5.3 are each right on their own content.
3. **Example 1-17's numeral** `#acge` decodes mechanically to 1375 (a=1, c=3, g=7, e=5); the transcription is verified against the source, so the gloss is corrected to 1375 wherever it says otherwise at Stage 3.

## Unresolved — for Paul (§7)

Both items settled 17 Sep 2026 as the comparison resolved them (classification conventions, not rule readings): `BANA 7.4.1d` and `BANA 7.6.1` stay `judgement` — each carries a discretionary clause ("most appropriate location", "if necessary"); their lettered sub-items remain individually testable rows.

(`references/_text/braille-formats-2016.txt`, lines 12310–13356; 112 rule/definition/cross-reference rows + 32 worked examples. Two independent extraction runs — 151 rows/34 examples and 141 rows/27 examples — reconciled by re-reading the source at every disagreement (including rendering three PDF page images to resolve Samples 16-3/16-8/16-12's mid-sequence line numbering, and the 13 bare-heading rows' `kind` naming); see the task's `compare-16/differences.md`, kept with the session's working files, for the full account. `BANA 16.12` (“Samples”, a page-locator index of the 13 Samples already extracted individually below) is excluded, matching the precedent already set for `BANA 4.12`/`BANA 8.12`. Stage 2 (Assess) complete 17 Sep 2026: every row has a status against `Emboss/format/document.mjs`, `input/parse.mjs`, `input/nimas-export.mjs`, `web/editor/editor.mjs` and existing tests, with several statuses grounded in scratch reproductions run against real liblouis (BANA 40x25) rather than just reading the code. No gold examples exist yet for §16 (Stage 3) — the worked Example/Sample rows above are left unassessed (no status column) pending that stage, per the pilot's own table shape. Findings are drafted in the task's `assess-16/notes-writeup.md` (F-106…, pending merge into `standards-findings.md` and renumbering) and questions in `assess-16/questions-16.md` (Q-34…, pending merge into `standards-questions.md`).)

## UKAAF B004, §11 + Appendix D — Notes and footnotes
(`references/_text/B004.txt`, lines 284–326 (§11, “Notes and footnotes”) and 506–537 (Appendix D, “Footnotes and endnotes” — not covered by either extraction run; extracted fresh for this task); 11 rule/definition/cross-reference rows + 2 worked examples (§11 only — Appendix D has none of its own). §11 has no numbered sub-rules of its own — a bare section title, an unlettered guiding-principles sentence, a shared ‘Good practice examples’ caption (folded into Example 1's own row, not given a row of its own, matching the B004 5 precedent for its analogous caption), two worked examples, and a closing cross-reference to Appendix D — so every §11 id below except the bare title (`B004 11`, kept per the `B004 5`/`B004 A` precedent) is a short descriptive tag, not the standard's own numbering. Appendix D likewise has no numbered sub-rules: a bare title, one rationale-plus-exception paragraph, a shared caption (folded, same convention), and six bulleted good-practice items, each its own row. Two independent extraction runs covered §11 (4 rows/2 examples and 4 rows/2 examples, differing only in row-splitting/naming, not content) reconciled by re-reading the source; see `compare-16/differences.md` for the full account, including Appendix D's fresh extraction. ## BANA Braille Formats 2016, §5 — Typeforms
(`references/_text/braille-formats-2016.txt`, lines 3794–4348; 70 rows: 50 rule/definition/cross-reference/not-applicable rows + 20 worked examples. Two independent extraction runs — 68 rows/20 examples and 70 rows/20 examples — reconciled by re-reading the source at every disagreement, including rendering the actual PDF pages (not just the .txt's own layout) where the text alone was ambiguous: `BANA Sample 5-3`'s page numbers and braille array were wrong in one run (its caption placed on print page 5-15 instead of 5-16, with the braille array wrongly padded with the wrong page's footer/filler) and are corrected here after rendering PDF pages 141–143 directly; `BANA Example 5-2`'s three braille lines, which read like plain print rather than this document's usual computer-braille ASCII, were settled — not guessed — by measuring the braille cell dot-patterns on the rendered PDF page (129, 800dpi) and confirming they correctly spell "dis-"/"ible"/"-ance" letter-by-letter in uncontracted braille. A run-A data bug (bare-heading rows 5.1–5.9 tagged `definition` in its `rules.json` while its own summary claimed `not-applicable`) is also corrected, to match this map's existing bare-heading convention (`BANA 4.1`–`4.12`, `BANA 7.1`–`7.7`). See the task's `compare-5/differences.md`, kept with the session's working files, for the full account of every difference and its resolution. UKAAF B004 has no Typeforms section — checked directly against B004.txt's own table of contents (sections 1–12 plus an Appendix and a Glossary; nothing titled or covering typeforms/emphasis) and its body (the only place "Typeform indicator" is defined is a single Glossary entry, with scattered bold/italic/underline mentions in §5 Headings and §9 Paragraphs) — so this section has no B004 counterpart. **Stage 2 (Assess, 17 Sep 2026): every row now carries a status, code evidence and a test (or "none").** Counts (50 rule/definition/cross-reference/heading rows): 19 not-applicable, 10 done, 6 partial, 12 not done, 3 out of scope. Worked examples (20): 6 done, 11 not done, 2 not-applicable (print only), 1 not tried. Headline result: italics/bold/underline are wired end-to-end (parser → document formatter → real liblouis UEB table), with symbol/word/passage-scope indicators and terminators verified directly against real `formatDocument` + liblouis output (BANA 40×25) in a scratch probe (no repository test yet covers this). But UEB's **script** typeform and the **five transcriber-defined typeform indicators** that BANA 5.1.4/5.5.1–5.5.3/5.9.1 require are *fully implemented in the bundled liblouis UEB table* (`liblouis/tables/en-ueb-g1.ctb` lines 88–164: `emphclass script`/`trans1`–`trans5`, each with its own symbol/word/passage signs and terminator) yet **completely unreachable from Emboss's own code** — `TYPEFORM` in `engine/louis.mjs`/`engine/louis-browser.mjs` exposes only 3 bits (italic/underline/bold), the parser and table-cell markup DSL never set a 4th, and the editor's toolbar has only Bold/Italic/Underline — confirmed both by exhaustive grep (zero matches for "smallcap"/"script"-as-typeform/"color" detection anywhere in `parse.mjs`) and by a probe that injects `tf=8`/`tf=32` directly and shows liblouis correctly emitting the script/transcriber-defined-1 signs, proving the gap is Emboss's plumbing, not the engine (see `standards-findings.md` F-86). A second, separate finding (F-87): `formatHeading`'s unconditional `stripEmphasis` (already flagged for headings generally in F-41) also blocks 5.3.1's "retain when partially emphasized" exception and 5.4.2's title/preposition worked examples. Findings F-86…F-92 and open questions Q-24…Q-27 are in this task's scratch folder (`assess-5/typeforms-writeup.md`, `assess-5/questions-5.md`), pending merge into `standards-findings.md`/`standards-questions.md`.)

## Unresolved — for Paul (§5)

All settled 17 Sep 2026 while reconciling the two extraction runs (data-quality and classification-convention questions, not open rule readings needing a transcriber):

1. **Bare-heading rows (`BANA 5.1`–`5.9`)** were tagged `kind: "definition"` in run A's `rules.json`, contradicting run A's own summary (which claimed `not-applicable`). Resolved to `not-applicable`, matching this map's existing convention for bare headings (`BANA 4.1`–`4.12`, `BANA 7.1`–`7.7`).
2. **`BANA Sample 5-3`'s page numbers and braille array were wrong in run B** (caption placed on print page 5-15 instead of 5-16; the braille array padded with 6 lines of the wrong page's footer/filler). Corrected by rendering the actual PDF pages 141–143 directly — see `compare-5/differences.md` item 12.
3. **`BANA Example 5-2`'s three braille lines** ("dis-", "ible", "-ance") read like plain print rather than this document's usual computer-braille ASCII. Settled — not guessed — by measuring the dot-patterns on the rendered PDF page (129, 800dpi): genuine, correct, uncontracted braille, spelling each fragment letter-by-letter exactly as printed.

Nothing here needs a transcriber; every question was answered from the source text and the rendered PDF pages themselves.


## BANA Braille Formats 2016, §9 — Displayed Material, Attributions, and Source Information
(`references/_text/braille-formats-2016.txt`, lines 6525–7190; 87 rows: 68 rule/definition/cross-reference
rows + 19 worked examples (8 inline Examples 9-1 through 9-8, 11 numbered Samples 9-1 through 9-11).
Two independent extraction runs — 87 rows/19 examples and 79 rows/19 examples — reconciled by
re-reading the source at every disagreement; the 8-row gap was entirely the bare section headings
9.1–9.7 and the "9.8 Samples" index, which one run gave their own not-applicable rows (kept here,
matching this map's own §7 precedent) and the other run skipped outright. Every quote (all 87 rows)
and every braille array (all 19 examples/samples, 154 braille lines) was independently rebuilt from
`braille-formats-2016.txt` by script and verified byte-for-byte; three `testable` classification
calls, the two runs' incidental-margin handling (an 8-space page-layout artifact stripped from
Examples 9-4 through 9-8, cross-checked against the section's own cell-margin rules), and Sample
9-11's page-break handling (footer/blank lines excluded, its form-feed recorded in `notes` rather
than kept in the braille array) are resolved in `compare-9/differences.md`, kept with the session's
working files. Stage 1 only (Extract) — every row's Emboss status/Evidence/Tests is `—`, assessed
next.)

text and applying this map's own existing conventions (see `compare-9/differences.md` for the full
account); nothing in §9 or B004 Appendix G needs Paul's input. Three `testable` classification calls
were settled by this comparison rather than left as open questions — `BANA 9.1.3` and `BANA 9.6.1`
to `not-applicable` (rationale/lead-in sentences with no independent instruction of their own, on

respectively), and `BANA 9.4.1c` to `judgement` (matching the same section's own `BANA 9.3.1e` and
`BANA 9.6.1b` font-attribute-distinction clauses).

## UKAAF B004, Appendix J — Poetry
(`references/_text/B004.txt`, lines 811–901; 8 rows: 3 rule, 3 definition, 2 worked examples.
This is the UKAAF material that pairs with BANA §13: a short guiding-principle sentence, then two
“Good practice example of poetry” units (line by line method; line indicator method), each a
sub-heading + rule paragraph + worked “Example:” with real braille (both illustrating Edward
Lear's “The Owl and the Pussy-Cat,” public domain, now quoted verbatim per this task's
instruction). Two independent extraction runs - 6 rows and 5 rows - disagreed substantially on how
to slice the two “Good practice example...” units; reconciled by giving each sub-heading its own
standalone not-applicable row (matching this map's own `B004 G examples-heading` precedent in §9,
rather than gluing the heading text onto either the following rule or the following example as
both runs had done) - see `compare-13/differences.md` §11 for the full account. The line-by-line
example's own “Or:”-introduced second braille rendering, and both examples' mid-example
page-break footers (page 26/27 and 27/28), are handled the same way as their BANA §13 counterparts
above. Stage 2 (Assess) complete 17 Sep 2026: every rule/definition row has a status against
`Emboss/format/document.mjs` and existing tests; the two worked-example rows are left
unassessed pending Stage 3 gold examples, matching §13's own table shape. Findings in
`assess-13/poetry-writeup.md` (F-128, F-129), questions in `assess-13/questions-13.md` (Q-46).)

## Unresolved — for Paul (§13)

Both settled 17 Sep 2026 (map conventions): a section's "Samples" index gets no row (§9's single not-applicable row stays as a harmless exception); rules of the form "follow print … on the Special Symbols page, or in a transcriber's note" are `exact` — the required outcome is fixed even though the transcriber picks the vehicle.

(`references/_text/braille-formats-2016.txt`, lines 1390–2934; 255 rows: 207 rule/definition/cross-reference rows + 48 worked examples (18 inline Examples 2-1 through 2-18, 20 numbered Samples 2-1 through 2-20, Sample 2-21's six component front-matter pages each as their own row, and 4 unnumbered "Sample"/"Samples" call-outs embedded in 2.3.7a, 2.6.1c, 2.6.1d and 2.8.1a). ## UKAAF B004, §1–4 + Appendix H — Identification and contents pages
(`references/_text/B004.txt`, lines 57–133 (§1 "Introduction" through §4 "Identification") and 732–795 (Appendix H, "Tables of contents"); 28 rows: 23 rule/definition/cross-reference rows + 5 worked examples. §1–4 have no numbered sub-rules of their own — bare section titles, unlettered guiding-principles/scope paragraphs, and (in §2/§3) bulleted objectives/getting-started items — so every id below except the four bare titles (`B004 1`, `B004 2`, `B004 3`, `B004 4`, kept per the `B004 5`/`B004 11`/`B004 E heading`/`B004 G heading` precedent) is a short descriptive tag, not the standard's own numbering; each bulleted objective/recommendation in §2/§3 is its own row (`B004 2a`-`2d`, `B004 3a`-`3h`). Appendix H likewise has a bare title, an unlettered guiding-principles paragraph, and two "Good practice example" call-outs (single-volume, multi-volume), the first of which further splits into its own bulleted layout guidance plus a worked print/braille sample. Two independent extraction runs — covering §1–4 fully but differing on whether §2/§3's bullets were extracted at all (one run folded them into a single heading row; the other extracted all twelve) — were reconciled by combining both runs' genuine finds (bare headings from one, bullets from the other) rather than picking a side; Appendix H was extracted fresh by both runs since neither existing pilot section had covered it. See `compare-2/differences.md` for the full account, including the `B004 1` conformance-paragraph split (a normative "must conform" sentence versus a separate resource-pointer sentence naming the purchasable RNIB Braillists' Manual) and the `B004 4`/`B004 H` heading-versus-guiding-principle boundary fix. Stage 1 only (Extract) — every row's Emboss status/Evidence/Tests is `—`, assessed next.)

## Unresolved — for Paul (§2)

None. Every difference between the two extraction runs for both BANA §2 and B004 §1–4/Appendix H — row-count and id-style variations, boundary placements between a rule statement and its embedded sample, cross-reference attribution, testable classifications, and the braille-array line-number/U+2800/"(Return to Text)" cleanup — was resolved by re-reading the cited source lines and, for the testable calls, by applying this map's own existing precedent (`BANA 11.2.5e`'s "fits on a page" → judgement; `BANA 1.17.1`'s "agency decision" → judgement; `BANA 9.3.1`'s definition → not-applicable; see `compare-2/differences.md` for the row-by-row account). One genuine extraction bug was found and fixed (one run's `2.3.7`/`2.3.7a` boundary had cut a source sentence in half at a PDF line wrap) and one shared erratum in both runs' braille arrays was found and fixed (Samples 2-17/2-18/2-19/2-20 each wrongly kept a trailing "(Return to Text)" footer line as braille content). Nothing here needs a transcriber's judgement or Paul's sign-off beyond what is already recorded.

## BANA Braille Formats 2016, §12 — Sidebars
(`references/_text/braille-formats-2016.txt`, lines 9993–10213; 22 rows: 15 rule/definition/
cross-reference rows + 7 worked examples (all BANA — UKAAF B004 has no Sidebars section, confirmed
directly against `B004.txt`'s own table of contents, which has nothing titled or covering
sidebars, and its body, which has zero matches for "sidebar"). Two independent extraction runs —
22 rows/7 examples and 18 rows/7 examples — reconciled by re-reading the source at every
disagreement, including viewing the rendered PDF page images already saved in one run's own
scratch folder to settle two prose-description errors (Sample 12-1's "two columns of running
text", corrected to one column with a sidebar box in the other zone; Sample 12-3's "five bulleted
steps", corrected to four, matching the braille's own four bulleted items) and one colour mislabel
(Sample 12-4's sidebar banner, corrected from orange to red); see the task's
`compare-12/differences.md`, kept with the session's working files, for the full account. The four

## Unresolved — for Paul (§12)

None. Every difference between the two extraction runs — the four bare-heading rows, two
`testable`/`kind` classifications (`BANA 12.1.1`, `BANA 12.2.1`, `BANA 12.3.1g`), the print-only
Samples' `lines` ranges, and several `describes` prose corrections — was resolved either by the
task brief's own explicit instruction, by this map's existing precedent elsewhere (`BANA
4.1.2`/`5.1.6` for the rationale-paragraph convention; `BANA 12.3.1a`/b/d for the discretionary-
trigger convention), by direct re-reading of the source text, by a mechanical script comparison
(`compare-12/verify_*.py`, zero mismatches), or by direct inspection of the rendered PDF page
images already saved in one extraction run's own scratch folder. One genuine convention question
was settled internally rather than left open: whether a print-only Sample's `lines` range should
include its trailing blank filler lines (as `BANA Example 9-1`/`9-2` did) or stop at the caption
(as `BANA Example 5-5`/`5-6` did) — this map already has both conventions in different sections.
Settled here using this section's own already-agreed rows as evidence (`BANA 12.3.1`/`12.3.1a`
already skip an identically-shaped blank-plus-footer gap without attaching it to either row), so
the five print-only Samples (12-1, 12-2, 12-4, 12-5, 12-6) use caption-only ranges. If Paul prefers
the other convention, those five ranges would each extend four lines further; nothing else in the
section depends on the choice.

## BANA Braille Formats 2016, §6 — Illustrative Materials
(`references/_text/braille-formats-2016.txt`, lines 4349–5344 (numbered body 4366–5338); 125 rows: 102 rule/definition/cross-reference/not-applicable rows + 23 worked examples (72 rule, 7 definition, 8 cross-reference, 15 not-applicable). Two independent extraction runs — 112 rows/23 examples and 125 rows/23 examples — reconciled by re-reading the source at every disagreement, including checking disputed "(See Sample …)"/"Sample:" boundaries against the source's own indentation and verifying every quote's word count against a fresh reconstruction from the source lines by script. Bare numbered headings at every level (6.1–6.13, plus the label-only sub-headings 6.8.1 "Descendant Charts" and 6.8.2 "Ascending Ancestral and Pedigree Charts") are `not-applicable` rows, matching this map's own convention (`BANA 4.1`–`4.12`, `7.1`–`7.7`, `13.1`–`13.11`); `6.14` (the Samples index) is excluded, matching the precedent already set for `BANA 4.12`/`8.12`/`13.12`/`16.12`. `BANA 6.3.2`'s seven STEM description key terms (Brevity, Data, Clarity, Drill-Down Organization, Tables, Processes, Narrative Description) are each their own `definition` row, and `BANA 6.12.3b`'s (1)/(2)/(3) sub-points are each their own row, per this task's explicit instructions. One run (B) silently dropped the trailing "(See Sample …)" cross-reference sentence from three otherwise-correct quotes (`6.10.3`, `6.10.5`, `6.10.6`) despite its own claimed line range already covering it — caught by a word-count verification script and restored from the other run. Every Sample's and Example's braille array was rebuilt directly from the source by script for this merge, since neither extraction run actually followed this task's stated braille convention (margin/line-number field stripped by counting, U+2800 → spaces): one run kept every line completely verbatim (numbering, U+2800, and body margin all literal), the other converted U+2800 to spaces but deliberately left the line-number field untouched. Content was not in dispute — both runs' raw braille agreed line-for-line with the source, including the internal print-page breaks inside Sample 6-13 (between "Option 1"/"Option 2") and Sample 6-15 (between the two screenshots), and the "—New Braille Page—" markers inside Samples 6-14/6-16 — only the final formatting convention was fixed. UKAAF B004 has no Illustrative Materials section — checked directly against `B004.txt`'s own table of contents (sections 1–12 plus an Appendix, none titled or covering illustrations/graphics) and confirmed no other match for "illustrat*"/"graphic" as a section heading in its body — so this section has no B004 counterpart. See the task's `compare-6/differences.md`, kept with the session's working files, for the full account of every difference and its resolution. Stage 1 only (Extract) — every row's Emboss status/Evidence/Tests is `—`, assessed next.)

## BANA Braille Formats 2016, §22 — Bibliographies

_Comparison made by Gemini Pro (Antigravity) from a Gemini run A (14 rows) and a Sonnet run B (14 rows), 17 Sep 2026; merged rows verified in-session (every quote and braille line verbatim, full numbered coverage). Its differences record lists resolutions by category. Assessed (Stage 2) 17 Sep 2026 with probes against the real liblouis translator (BANA mode, 40×25) — a full-repository search for "bibliograph" finds no matches anywhere in the code, tests, or docs, so nothing below is bibliography-specific: every "done" row is satisfied by pre-existing generic mechanisms (nested-list margins, the shared segment/typeform pipeline, plain-text translation of an em-dash/hyphen substitution) built for other sections. See `bibliographies-writeup.md` and `questions-22.md` (pending merge into `standards-findings.md`/`standards-questions.md` as F-184/F-185 and Q-57/Q-58)._


UKAAF B004 has no matching section.

### Rules

| ID | Kind | Testable | Requires | Emboss status | Evidence | Tests |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| BANA 22.1 | definition | not-applicable | Bare subsection heading with no rule sentence of its own; the first rule under it is 22.1.1. | not-applicable | Heading, cross-reference, or example only. | — |
| BANA 22.1.1 | rule | not-applicable | Braille bibliographies, regardless of how varied their print appearance, are treated consistently in braille. | not-applicable | Rationale/context paragraph (matching this map's convention for BANA 4.1.2/5.1.6/12.1.1): states no independently testable transcription action of its own — the "treated consistently" outcome it describes is realized entirely by the specific rules that follow (22.2.x/22.3.x), assessed on their own rows below. | — |
| BANA 22.2 | definition | not-applicable | Bare subsection heading with no rule sentence of its own; the first rule under it is 22.2.1. | not-applicable | Heading, cross-reference, or example only. | — |
| BANA 22.2.1 | rule | exact | Each bibliography entry is listed using a 1-3 margin (first line at margin 1, runover lines at margin 3). | done | A bibliography has no dedicated element in Emboss — it can only reach the formatter as an ordinary unclassed `<list type="pl">` (`parseSingleList`, `Emboss/input/parse.mjs:2014-2077`, sets `detectedKind='plain'` for `type="pl"`). Its margins come from the fully generic `nestedMargins`/`listMaxLevel` (`Emboss/format/document.mjs:132`, `:420-424`), called from `formatList` (`document.mjs:515-552`): for a single-level list (every item at level 0) this reduces to `first:0, runover:2` — cell 1 / cell 3 — in BANA mode, for any list kind. Probe (scratch `probe22.mjs`, real liblouis, BANA 40×25): two entries built as a plain `<list type="pl">`, one with a long runover, format with the first line of each entry at cell 1 (0 leading spaces) and every runover line at cell 3 (2 leading spaces) — confirmed for entries encoded either as one shared `<list>` or as separate `<list>` blocks per entry (block-structure-independent, unlike 22.3.1/22.3.2 below). No bibliography-specific code exists; this is inherited unchanged from the mechanism BANA §8 lists/§10 exercises/§21 indexes already share. | none (no existing test uses a bibliography-shaped list; see scratch probe above) |
| BANA 22.2.2 | rule | exact | Punctuation and font attributes in a print bibliography entry are followed in braille. | done | List items carry ordinary `segments` (with `tf` typeform bits) through the same `segmentsToBraille` pipeline used by every other list (`document.mjs:746-`), already exercised for the general italic/bold-in-a-list-item case by `Emboss/format/test-deep-typeform-matrix.mjs`. Probe (`probe22.mjs`): an entry with an `<em>`-italicised book title (`Puzo, Mario. *The Godfather: A Novel*. Completed by Carol Gino. New York: Harper, 2002.`) formats with UEB italic indicators around exactly the italicised run and every comma/period preserved (`,PUZO1 ,M>IO4 .7,! ,GOD"F3 ,A ,NOVEL.'4  ,COMPLET$ BY ,C>OL ,G9O4 ,NEW ,YORK3  ,H>P]1 #BJJB4`) — no bibliography-specific code involved, inherited from the shared segment/typeform mechanism. | none |
| BANA 22.2.3 | rule | exact | When print substitutes a long dash for a repeated author's name (two or more consecutive works by the same author), braille uses the long dash, spaced as in print; if print uses a different symbol for this substitution, braille follows print instead. | done | No dash-substitution code exists anywhere (confirmed by grep of `format/`/`input/` for "dash"/"emdash"/long dash handling specific to this rule) — the rule is satisfied precisely because nothing intercepts the character: whatever symbol print used for the substitution reaches the translator as ordinary text. Probe (`probe22.mjs`, `probe22b.mjs`): a literal em-dash (—) character replacing a repeated author's name translates via the ordinary UEB pipeline to `,-` — the long-dash sign — exactly matching BANA's own Example 22-2 (`",-4 #aiga4 ,canada's ,railroads4"`); a literal three-hyphen dash (`---`, BANA Example 22-3's own alternate symbol) passes through unchanged as `---4`, an exact character match against Example 22-3's own quoted braille (`"---4 .7,h>ry ,pott] & ! ,prison] ("`, case aside). Both symbols "follow print" automatically with zero special-casing. | none |
| BANA 22.2.4 | rule | exact | A bibliography written entirely in a foreign language is transcribed in uncontracted braille, using the foreign-alphabet symbols appropriate to that language. | not done | `engine/louis.mjs`'s `TABLES` (lines 13-17) wires up only three English UEB tables; no language-table switching exists anywhere, and `xml:lang` (read once, `input/parse.mjs:1411`, for `doc.lang`) is never consulted by the formatter/translator to change table or mode. The generic `uncontracted` segment mechanism (`document.mjs:746-`, `o.translateG1`) can be hand-applied via `class="uncontracted"` and happens to give readable (though not genuinely French) results for a Latin-alphabet language (probe `probe22b.mjs`: `;;;,CAMUS1 ,ALBERT4 ,L',^/ETRANGER4 ,PARIS3 ,GALLIMARD1 #AIDB4;'` — letter-for-letter, no UEB contractions) but produces unreadable literal `\Xhhhh` escape sequences for a non-Latin alphabet (probe, Greek: `";;;,.O.M'\\X03AE'.R.O.U1"` etc.) — proving there is no path to a genuine foreign alphabet. With no markup at all, foreign text is translated with ordinary UEB Grade 2 English contractions, which is simply wrong. See `standards-findings.md` F-185 (pending merge) / `bibliographies-writeup.md`. | none |
| BANA 22.3 | definition | not-applicable | Bare subsection heading with no rule sentence of its own; the first rule under it is 22.3.1. | not-applicable | Heading, cross-reference, or example only. | — |
| BANA 22.3.1 | rule | exact | In an annotated bibliography, the bibliographic information uses a 1-5 margin and the descriptive (annotation) information uses a 3-5 margin. | partial | The generic `nestedMargins` formula (see 22.2.1) also happens to produce exactly 1-5/3-5 for a two-level list (`maxLevel=1`): level 0 → cell 1/cell 5, level 1 → cell 3/cell 5. Probe (`probe22.mjs`) confirms this **only** when the annotation is authored as a nested `<list><li>` inside the citation's own `<li>`. The identical text with the annotation left as continuous prose in the **same** `<li>` (at least as plausible an encoding of one continuous print paragraph, since DTBook has no "annotation" element) collapses to a single flat item at cell 1/cell 3 throughout — the 1-5/3-5 split is lost entirely (probe `probe22b.mjs`, test 8). Emboss has no signal anywhere for where a citation ends and its annotation begins. See F-184 (pending merge) / `bibliographies-writeup.md`. | none |
| BANA 22.3.2 | rule | exact | A bibliography mixing annotated and unannotated entries uses the 1-5, 3-5 margin scheme throughout (i.e., the annotated-bibliography margins are applied even to the unannotated entries). | partial | `listMaxLevel` (`document.mjs:420-424`) scans **one list block**, so an unannotated entry is only promoted to 1-5/3-5 when it shares that block with an annotated entry. Probe (`probe22c.mjs`): an unannotated entry ("Smith, John…") placed in the **same** `<list>` as an annotated one is correctly promoted to cell-5 runover (`"    ,PRESS1 #BJJA4"`) — satisfied only as a side effect of sharing `maxLevel`; the identical entry placed in its **own** separate `<list>` block (equally plausible, e.g. one `<list>` per entry) stays at cell-3 runover (`"  ,PRESS1 #BJJA4"`) — 22.3.2 violated. Same root cause as 22.3.1: no signal marks several list blocks as one bibliography. See F-184 (pending merge) / `bibliographies-writeup.md`. | none |

| ID | Illustrates | Emboss status | Evidence | Tests |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| BANA Example 22-1 | The exact braille shown must be produced for a print input matching what is described. | done (reproduced with an equivalent, not the exact, input — the example gives braille only, no print text is recoverable from it standalone) | Probe (`probe22.mjs`): two unannotated entries built as a plain `<list type="pl">` reproduce the illustrated 1-3 margin structure exactly (entry at cell 1, every runover at cell 3), matching BANA 22.2.1's evidence above. | none |
| BANA Example 22-2 | The exact braille shown must be produced for a print input matching what is described. | done (reproduced with an equivalent input) | Probe (`probe22.mjs`): a repeated author's name replaced by a literal em-dash translates to `,-`, the long-dash sign, matching this example's own quoted braille (`",-4 #aiga4 ,canada's ,railroads4"`); see BANA 22.2.3's evidence above. | none |
| BANA Example 22-3 | The exact braille shown must be produced for a print input matching what is described. | done (reproduced with an equivalent input) | Probe (`probe22b.mjs`): a three-hyphen dash substitution passes through unchanged as `---4`, an exact character match (case aside) against this example's own quoted braille line (`"---4 .7,h>ry ,pott] & ! ,prison] ("`); see BANA 22.2.3's evidence above. | none |
| BANA Example 22-4 | The exact braille shown must be produced for a print input matching what is described. | partial | Illustrates BOTH 22.3.1 (1-5/3-5 annotated margins) and 22.2.3 (long-dash substitution) together. The long-dash half reproduces correctly (see Example 22-2/BANA 22.2.3). The margin half only reproduces when the annotation is authored as a nested list item under the citation (probe `probe22.mjs`); a real print annotation is continuous prose, and nothing in Emboss's data model marks where the citation ends and the annotation begins (probe `probe22b.mjs` test 8 shows the split is lost when both are one `<li>`) — see F-184 (pending merge) / `bibliographies-writeup.md`. | none |

## Unresolved — for Paul (§22)

- **Q-57** (pending merge into `standards-questions.md`): how should Emboss know where a
  bibliography entry's citation ends and its annotation begins, and that several `<list>`
  blocks together form one bibliography, so BANA 22.3.1/22.3.2's 1-5/3-5 margin scheme is
  reachable for real (not just nested-list-shaped) input? See F-184.
- **Q-58** (pending merge into `standards-questions.md`): is genuine foreign-language
  braille (real per-language tables, chosen automatically from `xml:lang`) worth building for
  BANA 22.2.4, or is a lesser stand-in (or leaving it to the transcriber) acceptable? See
  F-185.

## BANA Braille Formats 2016, §15 — Line-Numbered and Line-Lettered Text

_Assessed by Gemini Pro (Antigravity) with probes against the real translator, 17 Sep 2026; merged in-session. Comparison made by Gemini Pro (Antigravity) from a Gemini run A (89 rows) and a Sonnet run B (80 rows), 17 Sep 2026; merged rows verified in-session (every quote and braille line verbatim, full numbered coverage). Its differences record lists resolutions by category._

(`references/_text/braille-formats-2016.txt`, lines 11773–12309. UKAAF B004 has no matching section. Two independent extractions merged. Stage 1 only.)
